newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 9.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Wednesday:

* American Brands Inc will spin off its Gallaher Tobacco business in Britain to shareholders within the next six to 10 months. It will also change its name to Fortune Brands and become a $4.5 billion maker of faucets, locks, whiskey and other varying products.

* Motorola Inc foresaw growth resuming in the semiconductor industry in 1997 and projected a charge of "several tens of millions" of dollars against earnings this quarter to cover the cost of cutting jobs.
* Germany's largest manufacturing companies like Daimler-Benz AG and Siemens AG have agreed to talk with unions about their plans to cut back on sick pay.
* Blockbuster Entertainment of Viacom Inc has agreed to buy Xtra-Vision video chain In Ireland and purchase a minority stake in PC Upgrades, which makes products to upgrade personal computers.
* Sony Corp announced a new management team to run Sony Pictures Entertainment, Columbia and Tristar Studios.
* Cadillac is spending $50 million on a three-month advertisizing campaign to convince baby boomers to buy its new Catera model.
* New York City is helping News Corp to get space for its new 24-hour news channel on Time Warner Inc cable systems in the city.

* U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission will consider a staff proposal to oblige companies that make use of Regulation S to disclose the terms of overseas stock offerings. The regulation used to exempt foreign offerings from disclosure.
* The National Association of Securities Dealers has filed an administrative complaint against brokerage house Sterling Foster & Co for allegedly defrauding investors.
* Microsoft Corp appears to be gaining ground against Netscape Communications Corp in the war over browser computer software programs for the World Wide Web.
* U.S. and Canadian economists win 1996 Nobel Memorial Prize in Economic Science.
* The Dow Jones industrial average rose again above the 6,000-point mark before falling on profit-taking to end at 5,966.77.
* U.S. Tresury prices slipped when an auction of new 10-year Treasury notes failed to interest buyers.
